stem: A particle has initial velocity $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and constant acceleration $3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Find its velocity after $3\,\mathrm{s}$.
A particle moves in a straight line with initial velocity $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and constant acceleration $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for $3\,\mathrm{s}$. Calculate its displacement.
A particle has initial velocity $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and constant acceleration $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Find its displacement when its velocity first reaches $10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
A particle starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for $5\,\mathrm{s}$, then travels at its attained constant speed for $2\,\mathrm{s}$. Calculate the total distance.
A particle moves at $8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in the positive direction and has constant acceleration $-4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for $4\,\mathrm{s}$. Find its total distance travelled.
State what the gradient of a velocity–time graph represents.

A velocity–time graph has a straight line from $0$ to $4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ over $2\,\mathrm{s}$, then a straight line to $-2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ over the next $3\,\mathrm{s}$. State the displacement over the $5\,\mathrm{s}$.
A particle has initial velocity $5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and constant acceleration $3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for $4\,\mathrm{s}$. Find its displacement.
On a velocity–time graph, what does the signed area between the graph and the time axis give?
